subject: Post-demo: security checklist, subprocessor roster & questionnaire kickoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@mediapulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — security next steps and subproc roster

Alex / Sara — thanks again for taking the time today. Great conversation; appreciate the clarity on latency targets and the sample traffic profile. As promised, a short recap and proposed next steps focused on security & third-party visibility so your procurement team can move fast.

Recap (call highlights)
- Use case: content moderation pipeline + ephemeral embeddings for search (PII redaction scoped)
- Latency target: 200ms p95 for short prompts; burst tolerance required for peak hours
- Required controls: SOC 2 Type II evidence, GDPR data processor assurances, and a short list of subprocessors for vendor scoping

Immediate next steps
1) I’m attaching a short security questionnaire (pdf) with core ask areas — if you can return it we’ll prioritize answers within 48 hours.
2) We’ve started a draft subprocessor inventory (csv) — Marissa will validate and hand over the most relevant entries for your legal team.
3) If you’d like, we can run a quick evidence package call next week (30 min) to walk SOC 2 items and data flow diagrams.

Attachments: redwood_security_questionnaire_v1.pdf (stub), subprocessor_inventory_draft.csv (stub)

Proposed times for a follow-up evidence review call: Tue 11/03 09:00–10:00 PT or Wed 11/04 11:00–12:00 PT — tell me what works and I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143
https://redwood.ai

From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@mediapulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Cheng <sara.cheng@mediapulse.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — security next steps and subproc roster

Karthik — thanks, this is perfect. I’ve looped Sara (procurement) — Sara, can you confirm if the attached questionnaire format works for you? We prefer a short written response for procurement, then the evidence call if needed.

Quick answers to help triage:
- SOC 2: we need confirmation you have Type II for the past 12 months or an in-flight audit report plus control mapping.
- GDPR: processor terms + DPA required; note that we will insist on deletion/retention controls.
- Subprocessors: please list any cloud infra partners, logging/monitoring vendors, and any analytics providers that see unredacted content.

Tue 11/03 09:00 PT works for me.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Reynolds
Security & Infrastructure Lead | Mediapulse
alex.reynolds@mediapulse.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@mediapulse.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sara Cheng <sara.cheng@mediapulse.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — security next steps and subproc roster

Alex / Sara — nice to meet you over email. I own our third-party mapping and evidence packages. A few clarifying points ahead of the 11/03 call so we can be efficient:

1) SOC 2 status: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II reports covering our hosted API and control plane through 2025; 2026 audit is in progress and we can provide an interim bridge letter plus control mapping for the specific services you’ll consume.

2) DPA / GDPR: we have a standard DPA (GDPR-compliant) and can share redlines; retention and deletion controls are configurable by deployment (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private).

3) Subprocessors: initial inventory below (high level). I’ll attach a CSV with more meta, but here are the key categories we expect Mediapulse to care about:
- Cloud compute: AWS (us-west-2) for hosted workloads; GCP used in a subset of model training pipelines (not in inference production for your planned config).
- Object storage: Amazon S3 (encrypted at rest, SSE-KMS option)
- CDN / edge: Cloudflare (DDoS + routing, no long-term storage of content)
- Observability: Datadog (metrics/traces) and Sentry (exceptions) — logs with PII are redacted by default in hosted mode; we can turn on stricter filters or provide dedicated logging captures in Dedicated/Private.
- Secrets / KMS: AWS KMS; optional HSM integrations for private deployments.

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_draft.csv (contains contact and purpose columns).

Prep for the call: if you can mark the rows that require evidence (e.g., SOC 2 coverage, encryption at rest, EU data residency), we’ll bring the relevant artifacts. Also, bring your legal team if you want to review DPA items live.

I’ll be on the 11/03 09:00 PT call. — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Sara Cheng <sara.cheng@mediapulse.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@mediapulse.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — security next steps and subproc roster

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of immediate clarifications from procurement/legal:
- Can you indicate which subprocessors would see unredacted user content by default in the hosted deployment? We are particularly concerned about any analytics or third-party model tooling.
- Please confirm the geographic regions used for storage/compute for hosted customers (we need EU residency options).
- For Datadog/Sentry: do you have any contract addenda or options for dedicated logging endpoints so those services don't receive raw text?

We’ll review the CSV and flag high-priority evidence rows by tomorrow. See you on Tue.

Sara

--
Sara Cheng
Senior Procurement Manager | Mediapulse

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@mediapulse.com>, Sara Cheng <sara.cheng@mediapulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — security next steps and subproc roster

Great — thanks for the quick feedback. Quick answers to Sara’s bullets so the call can focus on evidence:
- Subprocessors that may see unredacted content in hosted mode: by default none of the observability vendors receive full request payloads. Datadog and Sentry receive metadata and traces only; we can enable dedicated ingest pipelines for telemetry that strip user text. The only services that may see short prompts in exceptional troubleshooting sessions are our internal debug workflow (access controlled) and a customer-requested debug dump (requires explicit consent).
- Regions: Hosted: primary US (us-west-2) by default; EU residency available (eu-west-1) for customers requiring it — we can pin persistent storage to EU. Dedicated/Private options offer full region control.
- Logging/contract addenda: We have SOC 2 coverage references for our telemetry partners and can propose contract addenda for dedicated logging ingestion if needed.

Next: I’ll send a calendar invite for 11/03 09:00 PT and share a short agenda (evidence mapping + DPA redline review). If you want to accelerate, Marissa can push the relevant SOC sections to HubSpot before the call.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
